- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to avoid missing downward momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 1.0) and price is rising, model often overestimates — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the first 5–7 days of a new trend — apply a 2–5% upward bias to early forecast points.  
- After sharp spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 3–8% in next 3–5 days to allow for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating +/– >0.5), model tends to smooth too much — add 1–3% noise or slight upward bias to avoid lag.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum — adjust final 5–7 days upward by 2–5% if sentiment is positive and price is trending up.
